res.summary:
The precommit hash matches (23ff354b...). The headline result holds and survives every convention change I tested: 0 of the 2,318 unique configs pass G1-G5. My own recount from /tmp/df5w/df5_arr.npz gives single-gate passes G1 167, G2 23, G3 13, G4 0, G5 0, with 0 mismatches against df5_gate. I reran QQQ X30 and got the same figures (median 21.78%, p10 MDD -38.30%), and the three quoted "closest X30 points" also match. The gate code matches the precommit exactly. The REAL window is the same for QQQ and candidates (1986-01-02 to 2014-12-31). The 2-day delay, horizon cuts and liquidation tax are identical in dfe and dfk; dfk parity for QQQ is 0. Neutralization uses all paths with t >= 300 in each world. DEF3, LTT and GOLD have no calendar gaps. I re-implemented the A5 ladder independently, and it matches df5fam._ladder exactly (0 weight differences, 0 event mismatches on 6 X paths x 4 configs). The v1 held-path shift in BV has no look-ahead: beng's rec[:,1] is the level in force, so shifting it back 2 days gives the decision-day level.

Why "0 pass" is robust: the binding gate is the X-world drawdown margin. All 13 configs that pass G1-G3 have X p10 MDD 20-68% deeper than QQQ, against a required 10% shallower. The near-misses that do have a 10% DD margin in both X30 and X10 are A5 ladders. They are short of QQQ's return by at least 0.98pp/yr, and the convention changes below do not move them.

What is misleading: the secondary claim that in X30 no config beats QQQ on both return and drawdown even at zero margin is literally true, but it rests on a tie. A3|e1.00|c0.20|GOLD+LTT+DEF3|none is -0.005pp pair and +0.25% DD margin. Any of these flips it:
- passing NDX dividends through to TQQQ/QLD;
- a 1%/yr term premium on the bonds;
- measuring before tax.
The dividend change is supported by ETF data up to 2014, where actual QLD and TQQQ beat the model by 1.0 to 3.65%/yr.

The X-world drawdown finding is also largely built into the design. Removing the crash windows removes exactly the periods when bonds and defensive assets paid off. Together with zero-excess neutralization of bonds and gold, diversifiers in X can only cost return or add drawdown.

issues.what: The X30 claim 'no config has both paired median > 0 and a shallower p10 MDD, even at zero margin' rests on a tie, not a finding. The best point, A3|e1.00|c0.20|GOLD+LTT+DEF3|none, sits at pair -0.005pp and DD margin +0.25%. Several defensible conventions flip it to pair > 0 with a shallower DD. X10 is a similar tie (DD margin -0.04%). Only the zero-margin statement changes; G4 still fails because it needs a 10% DD margin.

issues.what: Leveraged ETFs are modelled conservatively: QLD = 2r-rf-1.70% and TQQQ = 3r-2rf-2.45% on the NDX price return. That is no dividends plus a 0.75% spread per borrowed unit on top of the 0.95% fee. QQQ itself gets the 0.55% dividend proxy, so every TQQQ-financed allocation is penalized by about 3x0.55% = 1.65%/yr per unit of TQQQ weight. This follows the precommit as written, but ETF data up to 2014 says it understates actual returns.

res.summary:
I reproduced the numbers with my own numpy simulator (/tmp/df5v/repro/sim.py and ladder.py; I did not call dfe, dfk, df5fam or run_job for any portfolio accounting). It matches df5_main.json exactly, so the computation is correct. Per path it matches /tmp/df5w/df5_arr.npz to within 3e-8, which is float32 storage precision. QQQ matches bit for bit. I checked all four requested items in X30, P30, P10 and REAL. Recomputed from the stored rows, the pre-registered result also holds: 2,324 configs, 2,318 unique, 0 pass all of G1-G5, single-gate counts G1 167 / G2 23 / G3 13 / G4 0 / G5 0. No stored config has paired median > 0 together with a shallower X30 p10 MDD, even at zero margin. The three quoted 'closest points' are correct.

The frontier claim is wrong outside the tested grid. The A3 grid only covers NDX exposure e >= 1.0 with diversifier weight c <= 0.5, and no other family pairs TQQQ with an equity sleeve at e < 1. In X30 my own TQQQ+QQQ+DEF3 mixes with e 0.6-0.8 and c 0.45-0.75 beat QQQ on paired median, median and p10 CAGR, and also have a p10 MDD 10-20% shallower (both with zero margin and with the 10% margin). They use the same 63-day rebalance, 0.3% cost and tax rules. Five of the 17 DEF3 mixes I tried pass G4. Two of them pass every gate G1-G5 in my simulator, and also pass H1 (cost x2) and H3 (P125):
- TQQQ .175 / QQQ .075 / DEF3 .75
- TQQQ .15 / QQQ .25 / DEF3 .60

Caveats on that finding:
- It is post-hoc. I picked these mixes after seeing the data, so they carry the same in-sample bias the precommit warns about and must not be adopted without a new pre-registration.
- It depends on the DEF3 rule. The precommit moves DEF3's mean to the SPX mean, but DEF3's volatility is about 11.6% against NDX's 20.7%. That gives DEF3 a higher excess-return-to-volatility ratio than NDX: 1.10 vs 0.92 in X, 0.57 vs 0.45 in P. If DEF3 is instead set to SPX's ratio, both mixes fail on return in X30, P30 and REAL. With raw, unshifted DEF3, the .15/.25/.60 mix still passes X30, but only by +0.08pp.
- Mixes using LTT, GOLD, GOLD+LTT(+DEF3), TBILL, SPX or VALUE sleeves at e 0.7-1.3 do follow the claimed frontier: none dominates QQQ in X30.

Conclusion: '0 of the pre-registered set pass' is true. 'Nothing beats QQQ in X30 on both return and drawdown' is an artifact of the grid boundaries, and it hinges on an assumption.

issues.what: The X30 'frontier' and 'no config has both' result comes from where the grid stops, not from the X30 world itself. A3 only spans e in {1,1.25,1.5,2} and c in {0.2,0.35,0.5}. No family combines TQQQ with an equity diversifier at NDX exposure below 1 (A1/A2 use DEF3 only as an unlevered QQQ L + DEF3 (1-L) split). Lowering e below 1 with a large DEF3 sleeve gives higher return and a shallower p10 MDD at the same time. Two simple static mixes outside the grid pass all of G1-G5.

I checked the claimed counts myself and they hold on the pre-registered grid. Running df5gate.analyse() on df5_main.json plus /tmp/df5w/df5_arr.npz gives N_raw 2324, N_unique 2318, single-gate passes G1 167 / G2 23 / G3 13 / G4 0 / G5 0, and 0 passers. In X30 and X10, no unique config has paired median > 0 together with a p10 MDD at least as shallow as QQQ's. Rerunning the 16 baseline configs I picked in X30 gave the json values exactly (for example A3|e1.00|c0.20|DEF3 pair +1.747pp, p10 MDD -39.0%; QQQ 21.78% / -38.3%).

The structural-limit test does not support the reading "no rule can beat QQQ on both in the crash-free world":

(1) Conventions are not what blocks a pass. I relaxed them one at a time and all together: dividends added to QLD/TQQQ (and to SSO/UPRO), cost 0, delay 1, tax 0, and raw un-neutralized sleeves. None of the 16 frontier configs reaches paired median > 0 with a p10 MDD 10% shallower than QQQ. The zero-margin claim is knife-edge, though. A3|e1.00|c0.20|GOLD+LTT+DEF3 sits at -0.01pp / +0.3% and flips to paired > 0 with a shallower drawdown under the dividend fix (+0.19pp / +0.5%), cost 0 (+0.04pp), raw sleeves (+0.21pp) and tax 0 (+0.43pp).

(2) What blocks a pass is the grid's coverage. The A3 static family only has NDX exposure e in {1, 1.25, 1.5, 2} and sleeve weight c in {0.2, 0.35, 0.5}, and the A1/A5 DEF3 mixes use no leverage. Off-grid levered defensive mixes run through the unchanged DF5 engine (tax 22%, cost 0.3%, delay 2, 63-day rebalance, TQQQ without dividend, DEF3 neutralized) pass both G4 and G5. Example: TQQQ 0.20 / DEF3 0.80 (A3 builder with e=0.60, c=0.80) gets X30 median 23.12% vs 21.78%, paired +1.43pp, p10 CAGR 19.01% vs 16.67%, p10 MDD -31.2% (18.5% shallower). In X10 the same mix gets paired +2.83pp with a drawdown 17.8% shallower. With raw DEF3 it still passes G4, but only just: paired +0.13pp, drawdown 16.7% shallower. I tested these mixes only in X. They are post-hoc, cannot become candidates, and I did not check them against G1-G3.

(3) Volatility timing really cannot do it in X30, even with no frictions. Frictionless pre-tax vol targeting on NDX with a 1-day lag is dominated by plain constant leverage: at the same p10 MDD it earns about 1.8-2pp less. The 1998-99 run-up alone accounts for -1.7%/yr of the -2.1%/yr timing loss. Recomputing with continuous source-calendar volatility gives the same result, so the joins between 250-day blocks are not the cause. In P30 the same vol-targeting rules pass easily, for example paired +3.78pp with a drawdown 22% shallower.

E5 theory:
- X drops each NDX crash from peak to trough + 250 days but keeps the run-ups before the crashes (1987 H1, 1996-99). So it selects on NDX's own outcome, and high volatility in X points to high returns rather than to danger. Any rule that cuts NDX exposure on a trend, volatility or drawdown signal gives up return in exactly those run-ups and has no crash left to avoid.
- Bonds and gold neutralized to zero excess return are also uncorrelated with NDX in X (correlation -0.05 to 0). They only add variance: the best (tangency) portfolio of NDX plus these improves the Sharpe ratio by 0.9%. Beating QQQ's drawdown by 10% at equal return needs roughly 11% more Sharpe, plus about 1.2-1.8%/yr per unit of leverage bought through TQQQ.
- The only way through is a sleeve with a higher Sharpe ratio than NDX. Neutralized DEF3 has 12.8% excess return at 11.6% volatility (Sharpe 1.10, vs QQQ 0.92; raw 0.98), with correlation 0.68 to NDX. Levering a DEF3-heavy mix through TQQQ does beat QQQ on both.
- So the zero is a fact about the timing rules tested and the grid boundaries, not an economic impossibility. The one route that works rests on DEF3's in-sample low-volatility premium, which the equity-neutral convention enlarges (in X it lifts DEF3 by 1.44%/yr).

- The three "closest X30 points" are exact.

- P-world construction (only X was rebuilt independently).
- Track B values (taken from stored arrays, never recomputed).
- Source-data splices (KF industries to SPDR for DEF3, synthetic LTT and gold, rf). Only QQQ/QLD/TQQQ were calibrated against ETF data.
- No look-ahead in the v1 held path.

CONTRADICTED OR MISLEADING: the generalisation "no rule beats QQQ on both in all three bases".

(2) The changes_conclusion=true issue on grid coverage (repro, limit) is credible, and I confirmed it with the UNCHANGED DF5 engine and gate code, which neither verifier did across all worlds. I fed off-grid configs to df5run.job's own A3 builder with e < 1:
- e0.70/c0.60 DEF3 (TQQQ .15 / QQQ .25 / DEF3 .60) passes G1-G5, H1 (cost x2) and H2 (delay 4).
- e0.60/c0.75 (TQQQ .175 / QQQ .075 / DEF3 .75) passes the same.
- In a step-0.05 neighbour scan, 4 of 7 neighbours also pass all five gates, so this is a region, not a single point.
The audit/limit "zero-margin tie" issue is also credible: two verifiers independently got the same flips. Given the off-grid passers it is moot anyway.

(3) STILL UNVERIFIED AND MATERIAL:
- Whether DEF3's in-sample low-volatility premium is real. The off-grid pass depends on it: it fails under Sharpe-neutral DEF3 (repro); with raw DEF3 the X30 margin is only +0.08pp.
- Source-data integrity of the DEF3, LTT and GOLD series.
- Independent rebuild of the P world.
- Placebo and selection-stability tests (section 6) for any passer.
- Any truly independent data. All three bases come from one 1986-2014 NDX history, so a pass is not three confirmations.

(4) VERDICT: The narrow statement holds and is robust: none of the 2,318 pre-registered rules beats QQQ on both return and drawdown in all of REAL, simulation and crash-free. The binding wall is the X-world drawdown margin, and pure timing rules really do fail in X (limit's E4). The broad statement "no rule beats QQQ on both in all three bases" is NOT supported. Simple quarterly-rebalanced static mixes that keep NDX exposure at 0.65-0.70 through a 15-20% TQQQ sleeve and put 55-75% in DEF3 pass all five gates and H1/H2 under the precommit's own engine and conventions. The A3 grid simply stopped at e >= 1 and c <= 0.5.

That counterexample must carry these caveats:
- It was found post hoc.
- It rests on DEF3 (staples/utilities/health, mean-matched to SPX at roughly half NDX's volatility), whose high Sharpe ratio is an in-sample 1986-2014 feature. It fails if DEF3 is given SPX's Sharpe ratio.
- Its margins are modest: +0.8 to +1.3pp/yr, and the binding drawdown margin is 11.7% (P10) against the 10% required.
- In report-only pre-1986 S&P worlds the same mixes draw down more than the index. Those use a different benchmark, so this is only a hint.
- It cannot be adopted without a new pre-registration.

The user should therefore hear "0 of the pre-registered rules pass", not "no rule can".
